title: Processing a clause preserves fixed variables of the restriction
statement: Fix $n$, and let $\rho_0$ and $\sigma$ be restrictions on $n$ variables, let $\ell$ be a list of literals each paired with its position index in a clause, and let a decision-tree path be given. Suppose the variable $v$ is fixed under $\rho_0$, i.e. $\rho_0(v) \neq \mathrm{none}$. Then, after processing the clause's free literals against the path — which returns updated versions of $\rho_0$, $\sigma$, together with the remaining path and the accumulated auxiliary data — the variable $v$ remains fixed in the returned restriction $\rho_0$: its value there is again not $\mathrm{none}$. In other words, this process never frees a variable that was already fixed in $\rho_0$.
hypotheses_covered: v is fixed under the input restriction: ρ₀(v) ≠ none
inputs: a list of literals with position indices, a decision-tree path, and restrictions ρ₀ and σ on n variables
replaced:
If $\rho_0\,v \neq \mathrm{none}$, then after running
\texttt{SwitchingLemma2.processClauseLits} the resulting $\rho_0$ at $v$ is still not
$\mathrm{none}$; the routine never turns a set value into an unset one.
